heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a bold editorial hero with a full-bleed orange-led mesh gradient and layered typographic composition rather than a standard split layout. Keep the hero media-free to create a premium, high-confidence first impression, then use alternating feature sections with one dark high-contrast band later in the page. Add subtle grid lines and floating chips to suggest generative intelligence without relying on dashboard imagery. The CTA should be solid brand orange with strong contrast, while the headline should be large and dramatic at 60px+ to satisfy hierarchy and make the long product message feel authoritative.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is centered and text-first on a high-contrast orange field.
Trust uses a static logo strip immediately after hero for logos-first credibility.
Product section uses a split alternating spotlight format instead of a generic feature grid.
Pricing is presented as a highlighted comparison-style decision band, not a standard table.
Testimonials switch to a static 3-card grid to create a calmer proof rhythm after the product block.
Lead capture returns to a centered card to close with a distinct conversion surface.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance for professional AI image and video generation. See how creative teams use multimodal models to create high-quality visuals faster.

sections.backgroundTreatment: bold editorial color field with subtle grain and minimal floating model chips
sections.designNote: Content-first hero to satisfy warm traffic continuity. Headline answers what it is, subheadline answers who it is for, and the only CTA is a full-width orange solid button on mobile labeled exactly 'Get started'. Keep the hero dynamic through typography, spacing, and subtle abstract generation visuals rather than a split media panel.

Place trust immediately after the hero because proof type is logos and the traffic is warm. Use 3-6 recognizable logos in a clean, flex-wrap grid with restrained spacing. If logos are unavailable, fall back to a simple metric strip; otherwise keep it logo-led and highly legible.

Use two alternating product blocks, one for Seedream 4.5 and one for Seedance 1.5 Pro, because there are multiple product sections and each needs its own emphasis. Seedream should open with a visual-first split panel showcasing image quality, typography, and composition control. Seedance should flip the rhythm with a contrasting text-led panel plus a cinematic preview area to keep the page from feeling repetitive. Avoid a flat feature grid; instead use a spotlight feature and supporting bullets, with distinct visual treatment for image and video capabilities.

Because the source content includes pricing plans, use a compact highlighted decision band rather than a dense pricing table. Emphasize the two purchase paths side by side, with Seedance slightly more prominent if the video capability is the higher-intent path. Keep the CTA consistent and exact: 'Get started'.

There are 5 testimonials, so use a 3-card grid with one featured quote and two supporting cards, not a carousel. Prioritize buyer-relevant roles like Creative Director, Video Producer, and Art Director to reinforce fit. Keep card styling minimal and editorial to maintain credibility without visual noise.

End with a centered conversion card to create a clear finish after proof and pricing. This should be the strongest conversion surface after the hero, but still elegant and restrained. The CTA remains exactly 'Get started' and should be solid orange at 100% opacity, with full-width behavior on mobile.
Keep the footer minimal and utility-focused so it doesn't dilute the conversion arc. Do not introduce additional CTA language or competing paths.

blueprint.designPersonality: An editorial, high-trust B2B AI showcase with strong orange brand ownership, clean spacing, premium shadows, and logo-first credibility. It should feel like a serious creative platform for enterprise teams, not a flashy consumer AI demo.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use premium editorial product imagery and abstract AI visual panels rather than literal dashboards. Show clean model showcases, subtle generation previews, floating feature chips, and logo-driven trust bands. Keep the visual language modern, minimal, and production-focused, with enough contrast to distinguish image and video sections clearly.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and product-specific, so 48px keeps it strong without breaking across too many lines.

colours.colourReason: Use the brand’s locked orange as the primary identity color and CTA color, supported by neutral black, white, and soft grey from the brand palette for contrast and readability. This creates a distinct Techjockey-branded AI page without inventing a new palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width split hero with brand/logo at top-left, large bold headline, short subheadline/supporting line, and a compact bullet-value list beneath. Primary messaging is stacked vertically on a dark/high-contrast banner, with no secondary CTA in the hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with a strong hero, followed by a lead-capture form section, then feature/product sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing and modest contrast shifts rather than heavy visual complexity.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple content cards with restrained decoration, likely border or shadow-based rather than glassmorphism. Prioritize readable text blocks, short feature titles, and concise supporting descriptions over dense layouts.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One prominent primary CTA in the hero and repeated action prompts in downstream sections. CTAs should be high-contrast, concise, and conversion-oriented, with forms acting as the main conversion mechanism.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing section detected; pricing is absent or deferred. Use a request-demo or contact-sales pattern instead of self-serve pricing tables.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the reference; likely minimal utility footer if present. Do not depend on a content-heavy footer for conversion.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Brand/logo presence in hero; otherwise content is primarily text-led with limited media emphasis. If media is used, keep it secondary and aligned to the left/right of narrative content rather than full-bleed editorial imagery.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led product sections with a label, product name, headline, descriptive paragraph, then a list of capabilities. Best suited to progressive disclosure: top-level summary first, then a structured capability list below. Multiple products can be shown as separate subsections with distinct labels.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form placed directly after the hero, inside a prominent card-like container. Form should be short, business-oriented, and supported by hidden metadata fields for tracking/segmentation. This is a primary conversion block, not a side element.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, enterprise-style presentation with no obvious motion system. Any animation should be subtle and functional, such as lightweight section reveal or form feedback, rather than decorative.
componentPatterns: Bullet benefit list with tick icons
designNotes: Use a conversion-first layout with the form immediately visible after the hero.
Keep copy blocks short and scannable; use bullets for key benefits.
Maintain a high-contrast hero band for immediate impact.
Prefer structured information architecture over decorative storytelling.
Separate products into clearly labeled sections to support comparison and progression.
Use enterprise SaaS visual language: clean, direct, and utility-focused.

minimal utility footer with contact and navigation support
avoidPatterns: hero-only page that hides the rest of the content
grid inside grid layouts for features
empty black space or unfinished hero right side
secondary CTA competition in the hero
formless page when lead capture is expected
overly dense feature walls with weak readability
media-heavy hero that reduces message clarity
pricing tables that feel self-serve instead of consultative
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professional buyers evaluating advanced AI generation tools, so the design should lead with product clarity, credibility, and a strong request-demo path. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the top-of-page trust layer should prioritize logo-style proof over stats or testimonials. The content is solution-aware rather than cold, so the layout should quickly explain what each model does, then move the visitor toward quote or demo conversion. A split hero works best because it supports high-impact messaging while leaving room for trust signals and a clear CTA. The overall structure should stay balanced and readable, with simple feature cards, repeated CTAs, testimonials from relevant creative roles, and a consultative pricing/quote section.
